questions.stem: In the source, a text block's first and last content lines are indented by 12 spaces and its middle line by 16. The closing """ sits alone on the next line, indented by 8. What does the middle line of the string start with?

options.text: With 16 spaces, its 16 less none, since a closing line at 8, left of the content, switches the removal off
options.says: a delimiter on the left lowers the count that is removed; it does not stop the removal

options.text: With 4 spaces, its 16 less 12, since the closing line's 8 is left out of the count
options.says: the closing delimiter's line takes part in the count, so the smallest count is its 8, not the content's 12

options.text: With no spaces, its 16 less 16, since each line loses its own indentation whatever the closing line's 8
options.says: only the smallest count is removed from every line; the rest is essential and stays

options.text: With 8 spaces, its 16 less 8, since the closing line's 8 is included in the count
options.says: the closing delimiter's line counts, and its 8 is the smallest count here, so the middle line keeps 16 - 8 = 8

origin.section: Moving the Closing Delimiter Left Indents Every Line; Moving It Right Changes Nothing

questions.stem: In an editor that draws a tab as 4 columns, four lines of a text block start at the same column: three are indented with 12 spaces, one with 3 tabs. The closing """ ends the last of the four lines, one of the space-indented ones, on that same line. What does the string hold?

options.text: The space-indented lines keep 6 spaces, since the compiler counts each tab as two characters
options.says: a tab is never expanded; it counts as one character

options.text: The space-indented lines keep 3 spaces, since the compiler counts each tab as three characters
options.says: a tab is never expanded; it counts as one character

options.text: The space-indented lines keep no spaces, since the compiler counts each tab as four characters
options.says: the compiler can't know the tab width the editor uses; it counts each tab as one character

options.text: The space-indented lines keep 9 spaces, since the compiler counts each tab as one character
options.says: the tabbed line counts 3 and the others 12, so 3 characters go from every line

origin.section: A Tab and a Space Each Count as One Character

questions.stem:
A text block holds three lines:
    , then %s indented 4 spaces more than
      , then
    . It is filled with formatted("
  • a
    • \n
  • b
    • \n
  • c
    • "). Where does
  • b
    • start in the result?

options.text: 4 spaces in, since formatted() indents each line it inserts like the line holding %s
options.says: formatted() replaces %s with the value as it is; nothing re-indents the inserted lines

options.text: At column 0, since the compiler removes the 4 spaces in front of %s as incidental whitespace
options.says: those 4 spaces lie beyond the smallest count, so they are essential and stay, in front of the first item

options.text: At column 0, since formatted() inserts the value as it is, after the compiler has run
options.says: the 4 spaces before %s precede the first inserted line only; the line after each inserted line break starts at column 0

options.text: 4 spaces in, since the compiler applies the line's indentation to every line that %s turns into
options.says: the compiler is done with the literal before formatted() runs, and nothing re-indents the inserted lines

origin.section: At Run Time, Indentation Is Your Job: indent() and stripIndent()

questions.stem: A service reads an e-mail footer from a file that an editor saved with a line break at the end. Every line of the file is indented by 4 spaces. The code calls footer.stripIndent(). What does the result hold?

options.text: The lines without their 4 spaces, since the empty line after the final line break is blank and blank lines are not counted
options.says: the javadoc counts the last line even if it is blank

options.text: The lines without their 4 spaces, since stripIndent() strips leading whitespace like strip(), final line break or not
options.says: it removes the smallest count, and keeps relative indentation

options.text: The lines with their 4 spaces, since the empty line after the final line break is counted as the last line
options.says: the empty last line counts 0, as a closing delimiter at column 0 would, so nothing is removed

options.text: The lines with their 4 spaces, since stripIndent() leaves a string read from a saved file as it is
options.says: stripIndent() applies the rule to any string; a runtime string that ends without a line break is re-based

origin.section: At Run Time, Indentation Is Your Job: indent() and stripIndent()
